L9: # Title:Loquetier: A Virtualized Multi-LoRA Framework for Unified LLM Fine-tuning and Serving
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite5†Yuchen Zhang , cite6†Hanyue Du , cite7†Chun Cao , cite8†Jingwei Xu L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled Loquetier: A Virtualized Multi-LoRA Framework for Unified LLM Fine-tuning and Serving, by Yuchen Zhang and 3 other authors
L14: 
L15: cite9†View PDF L16: > Abstract:Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) has become a widely adopted parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) technique for adapting large language models (LLMs) to downstream tasks. While prior work has explored strategies for integrating LLM training and serving, there still remains a gap in unifying fine-tuning and inference for LoRA-based models. We present Loquetier, a virtualized multi-LoRA framework that seamlessly integrates LoRA fine-tuning and serving within a single runtime.
L17: Loquetier introduces two key components: (1) a Virtualized Module that isolates PEFT-based modifications and supports multiple adapters on a shared base model, and (2) an optimized computation flow with a kernel design that merges fine-tuning and inference paths in forward propagation, enabling efficient batching and minimizing kernel invocation overhead.
L18: Extensive experiments across three task settings show that Loquetier consistently outperforms existing baselines in both performance and flexibility, achieving up to $3.0\times$ the throughput of the state-of-the-art co-serving system on inference-only tasks and $46.4\times$ higher SLO attainment than PEFT on unified fine-tuning and inference tasks. The implementation of Loquetier is publicly available at cite10†this https URL†github.com .

L9: # Title:MISA: Memory-Efficient LLMs Optimization with Module-wise Importance Sampling
L10: 
L11: Authors:cite6†Yuxi Liu , cite7†Renjia Deng , cite8†Yutong He , cite9†Xue Wang , cite10†Tao Yao , cite11†Kun Yuan L12: 
L13: View a PDF of the paper titled MISA: Memory-Efficient LLMs Optimization with Module-wise Importance Sampling, by Yuxi Liu and 5 other authors
L14: 
L15: cite12†View PDF cite13†HTML (experimental) L16: > Abstract:The substantial memory demands of pre-training and fine-tuning large language models (LLMs) require memory-efficient optimization algorithms. One promising approach is layer-wise optimization, which treats each transformer block as a single layer and optimizes it sequentially, while freezing the other layers to save optimizer states and activations. Although effective, these methods ignore the varying importance of the modules within each layer, leading to suboptimal performance.
L17: Moreover, layer-wise sampling provides only limited memory savings, as at least one full layer must remain active during optimization. To overcome these limitations, we propose Module-wise Importance SAmpling (MISA), a novel method that divides each layer into smaller modules and assigns importance scores to each module. MISA uses a weighted random sampling mechanism to activate modules, provably reducing gradient variance compared to layer-wise sampling.
L18: Additionally, we establish an \(\mathcal{O}(1/\sqrt{K})\) convergence rate under non-convex and stochastic conditions, where $K$ is the total number of block updates, and provide a detailed memory analysis showcasing MISA's superiority over existing baseline methods. Experiments on diverse learning tasks validate the effectiveness of MISA. Source code is available at cite14†this https URL†github.com .

L11: # Title:Cognitive Alignment in Personality Reasoning: Leveraging Prototype Theory for MBTI Inference
L12: 
L13: Authors:cite6†Haoyuan Li , cite7†Yuanbo Tong , cite8†Yuchen Li , cite9†Zirui Wang , cite10†Chunhou Liu , cite11†Jiamou Liu L14: 
L15: View a PDF of the paper titled Cognitive Alignment in Personality Reasoning: Leveraging Prototype Theory for MBTI Inference, by Haoyuan Li and 5 other authors
L16: 
L17: cite12†No PDF available, click to view other formats L18: > Abstract:Personality recognition from text is typically cast as hard-label classification, which obscures the graded, prototype-like nature of human personality judgments. We present ProtoMBTI, a cognitively aligned framework for MBTI inference that operationalizes prototype theory within an LLM-based pipeline. First, we construct a balanced, quality-controlled corpus via LLM-guided multi-dimensional augmentation (semantic, linguistic, sentiment).
L19: Next, we LoRA-fine-tune a lightweight (<=2B) encoder to learn discriminative embeddings and to standardize a bank of personality prototypes. At inference, we retrieve top-k prototypes for a query post and perform a retrieve--reuse--revise--retain cycle: the model aggregates prototype evidence via prompt-based voting, revises when inconsistencies arise, and, upon correct prediction, retains the sample to continually enrich the prototype library.
L20: Across Kaggle and Pandora benchmarks, ProtoMBTI improves over baselines on both the four MBTI dichotomies and the full 16-type task, and exhibits robust cross-dataset generalization. Our results indicate that aligning the inference process with psychological prototype reasoning yields gains in accuracy, interpretability, and transfer for text-based personality modeling.
